hero.subtitle: Authorization Code Exchange for web and mobile — Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) setup, API reference, and frontend examples.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: Atlassian login is optional and controlled by ATLASSIAN_AUTH_ENABLED. When disabled, Atlassian endpoints return 503 Service Unavailable. JWTs are never placed in the redirect URL; the API issues a one-time exchangeCode (Redis, 60 seconds). The same POST /auth/exchange endpoint is shared with other social providers.
items: Profile fetched via GET https://api.atlassian.com/me after token exchange
Authorize params include audience=api.atlassian.com and prompt=consent
Same token response shape as POST /auth/login

console.title: Atlassian Developer Console
console.description: Create an app at https://developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/ → Create → OAuth 2.0 (3LO). Set the Callback URL to match ATLASSIAN_CALLBACK_URL. Add the User Identity API and scope read:me.
steps: Add the User Identity API and scope read:me
Copy Client ID and Client Secret into your .env
Ensure ATLASSIAN_CALLBACK_URL matches the Callback URL registered in the Atlassian console

env.title: Environment variables
env.description: Loaded from .env via src/config/atlassian-oauth.config.ts (namespace atlassianOAuth on ConfigService). See .env.example.

roles.title: Default roles for new Atlassian users
roles.description: New Atlassian users receive roles: [] by default (same as password register). Set ATLASSIAN_OAUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES in .env to a comma-separated list of Role values (e.g. user or user,manager). Existing users linked by email keep their current roles.

flow.title: Sequence
items: User consents on Atlassian; browser hits GET /api/v1/auth/atlassian/callback
API calls GET https://api.atlassian.com/me, upserts user, stores exchangeCode in Redis, redirects to redirect?code=...
Client POSTs { code } to /api/v1/auth/exchange and receives JWTs

start.title: 1. Start OAuth
start.description: Opens Atlassian consent at https://auth.atlassian.com/authorize with audience=api.atlassian.com and prompt=consent. Query redirect must match a prefix in ATLASSIAN_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST (or omit to use the first allowlist entry). Scope: read:me.

callback.title: 2. Callback
callback.description: Handled by the API. Token exchange uses https://auth.atlassian.com/oauth/token. Redirects to your app with ?code= (or &code= if the URL already has a query).

exchange.title: 3. Exchange code
exchange.description: Public endpoint shared with other social providers. Consumes the code (single use) and returns the same shape as login.

web.title: Frontend — Web (SPA)
web.description: Typical flow: button starts OAuth in the same window (or popup); a callback route on your frontend origin reads code from the query string and calls exchange.
notes: Add your frontend callback URL to ATLASSIAN_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST (e.g. http://localhost:5173/auth/callback)
ATLASSIAN_CALLBACK_URL must point at the Nest API, not the SPA
Store accessToken / refreshToken securely (memory + httpOnly cookie patterns as you prefer)

mobile.title: Frontend — Mobile (deep link)
mobile.description: Use a custom scheme (or universal link) in the allowlist. After Atlassian, the API redirects to myapp://success?code=.... The app opens, parses the code, and calls exchange.
notes: Register the scheme in the OS / Expo app.json
Exchange over HTTPS against your API base URL

security.title: Security notes
items: Redirect URLs must match ATLASSIAN_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST prefixes
Exchange codes are single-use and expire in 60 seconds (Redis)
Existing local users are linked by verified Atlassian email (atlassianId set; roles unchanged)
Atlassian-only users have password null — password login / change-password will fail until a password is set
Email is required from api.atlassian.com/me; login fails if Atlassian does not return an email (scope read:me)

userModel.title: User model
userModel.description: Postgres entity / interface fields used by Atlassian login:
items: atlassianId — unique nullable Atlassian account id (account_id from /me)
isActive — set true for new Atlassian users
